title: runWatchdog's isObsRecording treats an OBS-websocket connect/call failure identically to 'confirmed not recording', so a dead controller + transiently-unreachable OBS wipes the recovery state file WITHOUT finalizing -- defeating the T-047 done-when criterion in exactly the scenario it exists for
evidence: packages/meeting-bot/src/capture/watchdog.ts:96-106 (isObsRecording probe): `try { await obs.connect(...); const status = await obs.call("GetRecordStatus"); return status.outputActive; } catch { /* OBS unreachable -- nothing this tick can stop; not an error, just "not recording" */ return false; }`. Traced deterministically: when a state file exists, the controller pid is dead (isPidAlive=false, the exact 2026-09-24 16:30:56 failure), and this catch fires (OBS websocket down/timed out/restarting while OBS's recording engine may still be running), decideWatchdogAction(watchdog.ts:33-40) receives obsRecording=false and returns 'stale-cleanup', which tickWatchdog (watchdog.ts:73-75) turns into `probes.clearState()` with NO call to finalize. The one artifact the whole T-047 mechanism depends on (the state file) is now gone; the next tick sees state=undefined -> noop-idle forever. No test exercises runWatchdog's real isObsRecording wiring at all -- watchdog.test.ts only injects WatchdogProbes fakes, never the catch-swallows-uncertainty branch of the actual probe.
reproduction: Code trace (no live OBS needed): with a RecordState on disk and its pid dead, call the real isObsRecording probe against an OBS instance that is reachable-but-recording (to confirm baseline true), then against a closed/refused port (e.g. stop obs-websocket or point OBS_WS_URL at a closed port) while OBS's own recording is hypothetically still active -- the probe returns false either way, so tickWatchdog runs stale-cleanup + clearState in both the 'confirmed idle' and the 'cannot tell' case.
fix_direction: Distinguish 'confirmed not recording' (a successful GetRecordStatus call reporting outputActive:false) from 'could not determine' (connect/call threw). On 'could not determine', log and no-op (leave the state file in place for the next tick) rather than routing into stale-cleanup/clearState -- e.g. have isObsRecording return a tri-state (or have decideWatchdogAction accept an explicit obsStatus: 'recording'|'idle'|'unknown' and treat 'unknown' as noop, never as grounds to clear the one artifact recovery depends on).

title: isPidAlive only probes pid existence (process.kill(pid,0)) with no start-time/identity check in RecordState -- OS pid recycling after the original controller dies makes tickWatchdog permanently misread a dead controller as alive, so an orphaned OBS recording is never finalized
evidence: packages/meeting-bot/src/capture/controller-state.ts: RecordState carries only `pid: number` (no process start-time, creation-time, or any other identity marker); isPidAlive (controller-state.ts, signal-0 probe) returns true for ANY live process holding that pid number, not specifically the original controller. Windows recycles pids after a process exits (commonly within the same session under continued process churn). If the original controller dies (console closed) and, before the next watchdog tick, an unrelated process is assigned the same pid, decideWatchdogAction sees controllerAlive=true and returns noop-active (watchdog.ts:38 'if (controllerAlive) return { kind: "noop-active", state }') forever -- the exact 'dead controller, OBS still recording' case T-047 exists to catch is masked. No test in controller-state.test.ts or watchdog.test.ts exercises pid-reuse; both isPidAlive tests only check 'this process's own pid' (true) and an implausibly large pid (false).
reproduction: Not independently reproduced live (would require deliberately recycling a pid, out of scope for this check's instructions); traced from the type signature and decideWatchdogAction's unconditional trust of isPidAlive's boolean.
fix_direction: Record an additional identity signal in RecordState at write time (e.g. the pid's start time via a platform probe, or a short-lived heartbeat file the controller rewrites periodically) and have isPidAlive-equivalent logic reject a pid match whose observed identity doesn't match what was recorded, rather than trusting bare pid existence indefinitely.
